order: say hello and why you're calling
safety: never share your address, your school or a password
a message from a stranger: don't reply, tell a grown-up

little.twist: Two people need help, and you choose who first.
little.can_now: say hello and remember names, help first, include someone new and keep a promise

steps.say: Welcome to the village! People here have names, jobs and things they need. Let's meet them.
Say hello to the baker: touch her.
steps.done: "Hello! I'm Amara. I bake the bread."

steps.say: Now say hello to the miller: touch him.
steps.done: "Hello there! I'm Tomas. I grind wheat into flour."

steps.say: Who is the baker?

choices.why: That's Tomas the miller. Amara is the baker: look for her white hat.
Bobo is your buddy! The baker is Amara, in the white hat.

steps.done: Amara! Remembering names makes people feel special.

steps.say: Amara looks worried: "I have no flour for tomorrow's bread!" Tomas has flour at the mill.
Help first: pick up a bag of flour at the mill. Touch it.
steps.done: A big bag of flour!

steps.say: Now bring it to Amara: touch her.
steps.done: "Thank you! Now I can bake."

steps.say: Amara says thank you. What do you say?

choices.why: Helping first, without asking for something back, is how friendships start.
A smile and 'you're welcome' make people glad they asked.

steps.done: Amara smiles: she'll remember your kindness.

steps.say: Ana's apples have spilt, and Tomas is carrying a heavy sack. Who do you help first?

choices.why: You can't help everyone at once, but you can help one, then the next.
Picking up apples is something you can help with: start with one person.

steps.done: One at a time: both of them are glad.

steps.say: Help Ana first: touch her to pick up the apples.
steps.done: "Thank you! I'm Ana, the farmer."

steps.say: Look: Lina is new here. She sits alone on the bench by the fountain.
What can you do?

choices.text: Say hello, and ask her to play

choices.why: Being new is hard. A hello can make a friend.
Staring can feel unkind. A smile and a hello are better.

steps.done: A kind hello: the best start.

steps.say: Go and say hello: touch Lina.
steps.done: "Hello! I'm Lina. Do you like drawing?"

steps.say: You say: "I'll bring my {gift} tomorrow, and we can draw together!" That's a promise.

steps.label: the next morning
steps.say: Night falls on the village... and here comes the morning.
It's the next morning. Keep your promise: pick up your {gift}.
steps.done: Got them!

steps.say: Give them to Lina: touch her.
steps.done: Promise kept! Lina has a new friend: you.

steps.say: You met people, remembered a name, helped first and kept a promise. They're in your Connections Book now!

check.say: Someone new is all alone. You...

choices.text: say hello and ask them to play
helping without asking for something back
only helping if you get paid

check.say: You promised to bring crayons tomorrow. Tomorrow you...

name_it.title: Making friends
name_it.source: CASEL's relationship skills (making friends, cooperating, offering help)

little.try_real: With a grown-up: help someone at home first, without being asked, and keep one small promise this week.

sources.fact: Relationship skills: making and keeping healthy relationships, cooperating, and asking for or offering help.
Social skills at five predict how children do as young adults.

middle.twist: One more introduction: find who can help whom, by yourself.
middle.can_now: find out what people need, introduce people who can help each other, promise only what they can do and ask a mentor politely

steps.say: In the village, everyone needs something. Help, and keep your word, and people trust you.

lines.amara: Amara: "I bake bread. I need flour every morning."
lines.tomas: Tomas: "I grind flour. I need someone to buy it!"
lines.ana: Ana: "I grow apples. My old spade broke."
lines.ivan: Ivan: "I make tools. I need customers."

steps.say: Meet four people: touch each one and listen to what they need.
steps.done: Four new names in your book.

steps.say: What does Ana the farmer need?

choices.why: Listen again: her old spade broke.
Listen again: her old spade broke, and she needs a new one.

steps.done: A spade. Knowing what people need is how you can help.

steps.say: Ivan makes tools and needs customers. Introduce them: touch Ana, then Ivan.
steps.done: "Ana, meet Ivan: he makes spades!" Now they can help each other.

steps.say: Who can help Amara? Introduce her to the person who has flour: touch Amara, then them.
steps.done: Amara gets flour, and Tomas gets a buyer. Both win!

steps.say: Mr Okafor needs new shelves for his books. Who can build them? Introduce them: touch Mr Okafor first.
steps.done: Sam the carpenter will build the shelves. You worked it out!

steps.say: Amara asks: "Can you bring me a bag of flour by tomorrow morning?" Your morning is busy. What do you say?

choices.text: "I can bring it by lunchtime. Is that OK?"

choices.why: A promise you can't keep hurts trust. Promise what you can really do.
'Maybe' is hard to count on. Say what you can do.

steps.done: Amara: "Lunchtime is perfect."

steps.label: the next day, at lunchtime
steps.say: The morning goes by... it's the next day, at lunchtime.
It's lunchtime. Pick up the flour at the mill.
steps.done: Flour in your arms.

steps.say: Keep your word: bring Amara the flour.
steps.done: Right on time. Amara knows she can count on you.

steps.say: Omar mends clocks. You'd love to learn how. How do you ask?

choices.text: "Could you show me how you mend a clock, please? I could come on Saturday."

choices.why: Mentors are busy people. Ask politely, and say when you can come.
People like being asked to share what they know. Ask politely!

steps.done: Omar smiles: "Of course!"

steps.say: Omar says: "My first rule: check twice, fix once." His tip is in your Connections Book.
Sam the carpenter is deaf: he talks in sign language. How can you talk with him?

choices.text: Face him, smile, point and show

choices.why: Shouting doesn't help. Face him, smile, point and show.
Everyone can be a friend. There are lots of ways to talk.

steps.done: Sam signs "thank you": in many sign languages, a flat hand from the chin, forward. Now you know a sign too!

steps.say: A week later, your clock works! How do you thank Omar?

choices.text: "Thank you for teaching me: my clock works!"

choices.why: A thank you makes people glad they helped, and keeps the friendship warm.

choices.text: Ask for more lessons straight away
choices.why: Say thank you first. People like helping those who are grateful.

steps.done: Omar beams. Mentors love hearing it worked.

steps.say: You found what people need, introduced them, kept your word and asked a mentor. That's how trust grows!

check.say: Ivan makes tools. Ana needs a spade. You can...
Someone asks for something by tomorrow, and you can't. You say...

choices.text: "I can by lunchtime. Is that OK?"

check.say: How do you ask a mentor to teach you?

choices.text: politely, and say when you could come

check.say: Sam is deaf. You talk with him by...

choices.text: facing him, smiling, pointing and showing

name_it.title: People who count on you
lines: Introduce people who can help each other.
Promise only what you can do, then do it.
Many ways to talk: face, smile, point, show.
name_it.source: CASEL's relationship skills and Chetty et al. (2022), Social Capital, Nature

middle.try_real: With a grown-up: think of two people you know who could help each other, and ask your grown-up how to introduce them.

sources.fact: Friendships across different groups (economic connectedness) are among the strongest predictors of getting ahead in life.
sources.source: Chetty et al. (2022), Social Capital I, Nature 608

sources.fact: Relationship skills include cooperating, communicating clearly and seeking or offering help.
Mobilising others and working with others are entrepreneurship competences.

big.twist: A tricky message pretends to be from a friend.
big.can_now: build a network of all kinds of people, connect people who can help each other, protect their good name and stay safe online

steps.say: A network is the people you know, and who know you. The strongest ones have all kinds of people in them.

lines.mei: Mei: "I built a water pump. I need a buyer!"
lines.kenji: Grandpa Kenji: "I've kept bees for 60 years. I need jars for my honey."
lines.rosa: Rosa: "I make jars, but I've run out of clay."
lines.gemma: Gemma: "I study rocks. I know where the clay is!"

steps.say: Meet four people: touch each one and listen to what they need and what they know.
steps.done: Four very different people. Each knows something you don't.

steps.say: Mei built a water pump and needs a buyer. Who could use it?

choices.why: An oven doesn't need a water pump. Who needs water?
Think of who needs water: Ana's fields are dry.

steps.done: Ana! Her fields are dry.

steps.say: Introduce them: touch Mei, then Ana.
steps.done: Mei sells her pump, and Ana's fields get water. Win-win!

steps.say: Rosa needs clay; Gemma knows where it is; Kenji needs Rosa's jars. Touch Rosa, then Gemma, then Kenji.
steps.done: Clay for Rosa, jars for Kenji. One introduction can help three people.

steps.say: Grandpa Kenji is 80 and has kept bees for 60 years. Why is he a great person to know?

choices.text: He knows things nobody else knows

choices.why: Older people know a lot. People different from you open new chances.
Friends of all ages and backgrounds help you see more.

steps.done: People different from you know different things: that's what makes a strong network.

steps.say: You promised Rosa clay by Friday, but the clay pit is closed. What protects your good name?

choices.text: Tell Rosa early, say sorry and offer a new day
Say nothing and hope she forgets
choices.why: People trust those who tell the truth early.
Blaming others hurts your good name. Own it and fix it.

steps.done: Rosa: "Thank you for telling me. Monday is fine."

steps.say: A month later, Mei's pump waters Ana's fields. How do you keep in touch?

choices.text: Send Mei a thank-you postcard: "Ana's fields are green!"
Only talk to her when you need something
choices.why: Keep in touch when you don't need anything too: that's a real connection.
Connections fade without a hello. A thank-you keeps them warm.

steps.done: Mei pins your postcard on her wall.

steps.say: Someone you don't know messages you: "Be my friend! Send me your address and I'll send you a present."

choices.text: Don't reply, and tell a grown-up

choices.why: Never send your address to someone you don't know. Tell a grown-up.
Never send photos or details to strangers. Tell a grown-up.

steps.done: Right. Online, only friends a grown-up has approved.

steps.say: A message says it's from Mei: "Quick! Send me your password, I need it for the pump!"

choices.text: Never share a password: check with Mei face to face, and tell a grown-up
Send it: it's from a friend
choices.why: Anyone can pretend to be a friend. Nobody needs your password: tell a grown-up.
Never share any of a password. Check face to face, and tell a grown-up.

steps.done: Good: real friends never need your password.

steps.say: You'd like to start a honey stall. Who do you ask for advice, and how?

choices.text: Ask Kenji politely for ten minutes, with my questions ready

choices.why: A mentor saves you mistakes: ask the person who knows.

choices.text: Ask Kenji to do it all for me
choices.why: Ask for advice, then do the work yourself.

steps.done: Kenji: "Ten minutes? Let's make it twenty!"

steps.say: Kenji says: "Good things take time: bees make honey drop by drop." His tip is in your Connections Book.
When people trust you, they tell you about new chances: Amara says the builders at the Launch Site would love fresh bread!
A network of all kinds of people, connections that help, a good name and staying safe online. Well done!

choices.text: all kinds of people in it

check.say: You can't keep a promise. To protect your good name, you...

choices.text: tell them early and offer a new time

check.say: A stranger online asks for your address. You...

choices.text: don't reply, and tell a grown-up
a thank-you or a hello, even when you need nothing
only calling when you need something

name_it.title: A network you can trust
lines: Connect people who can help each other.
Tell the truth early: your good name matters.
Keep in touch, and say thank you.
Online: only friends a grown-up approved.
name_it.source: Chetty et al. (2022), Social Capital, Nature; CASEL's relationship skills

big.try_real: With a grown-up: draw your network: family, friends, teachers, neighbours. Who could you thank this week?

sources.fact: Economic connectedness, friendships between people from different backgrounds, is among the strongest predictors of upward mobility.
sources.source: Chetty et al. (2022), Social Capital I, Nature 608

sources.fact: Never share personal details or passwords with people you only know online; tell a trusted adult.
Leadership and social influence are among the skills employers rank highest.
sources.source: World Economic Forum, The Future of Jobs Report 2025
